title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 'Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines' versus Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text first states that T3 plants were grown under salt stress for 7 days and describes selection based on that period, but then states 'Comparative shoot-length, root-length and fresh wt. taken after 10 days-stress indicated...' for the same phenotypic comparison. Figure 3's caption explicitly says the plants were 'kept for 7 days.' Thus the same data/experiment is described as both 7 and 10 days of stress, which is contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 'Test of allergenicity for candidate protein(s)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors conclude from low identity matches (25.5% and 24.8%) to known allergens and an AllergenOnline search that the PcIMT1 alignments are 'indicative of non-allergenicity' and that PcINO1 'exhibited no allergenicity.' Bioinformatics searches only compare against known allergens and cannot establish that a protein is non-allergenic; absence/low similarity to known allergens is a screening criterion, not proof of safety. This overstates the evidence and could mislead readers.

The text repeatedly refers to a '37-amino acid specific PcINO1-transcript' or '37-amino acid specific PcINO1-transcript level expression.' A transcript is an RNA molecule and is not measured in amino acids; the authors likely mean a transcript region encoding a 37-amino-acid peptide/epitope or a 111-bp transcript-specific sequence. This is a fundamental molecular biology misdescription of the assay target.
